# Security Policy

## Supported versions

This is a small project with a single maintained line. Fixes land on `main`;
older tags are not patched.

| Version | Supported |
| :------ | :-------- |
| Latest release | Yes |
| Anything older | No |

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Don't open a public issue.** Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on
this repository: go to the **Security** tab and choose *Report a vulnerability*.
That channel is private until a fix is published.

Please include what you can of the following. Partial reports are still worth
sending — a rough report today beats a complete one that never gets written.

- What an attacker could do, and what they'd need to already have
- The file, function or step involved
- How to reproduce it, or the configuration that triggers it
- Your operating system and Python version

You can expect an acknowledgement within a week. If a report turns out to be
valid, the fix and the advisory are published together, and you're credited by
whatever name you ask for — or not at all, if you'd rather.

## What counts here

This project ships Python scripts that generate files and read folders. The
realistic risks are in that shape of work:

- A path in a config or an ignore file that escapes the folder it should stay in
- A generated file that writes somewhere it wasn't asked to
- A crafted `.skill-config.json` that makes the generator overwrite existing
  content — the generator refuses to overwrite by design, so a way around that
  refusal is a bug worth reporting

Skills generated by this boilerplate are your own work once written; their
contents are outside this project's scope.

## What doesn't

- Findings that need an attacker to already control the machine running the
  scripts
- Reports from automated scanners with no working reproduction
- Anything about Claude, Claude Code, or claude.ai themselves. Report those to
  Anthropic at <https://hackerone.com/anthropic-vdp>, not here.
